You are a professional game-mechanics analysis expert with long-term research on the rule systems, control patterns, action sequences, and hidden strategies of various new games. You are especially skilled at rapidly learning the core gameplay, movement rules, turning logic, skill trigger conditions, and hidden rules of a completely unfamiliar game by watching video.
Now you will watch a video context showing actual gameplay footage of a brand-new game. You must completely forget all pretraining knowledge and rely only on the game-rule text I provide next and the actual behavior shown in the video for learning and reasoning. Do not try to identify the specific game title, character model, or familiar elements in the video. You only need to focus on extracting the action sequence, timing, path, and result in the video, and make judgments strictly according to the rules I provide.
After the video ends, please accurately analyze and answer the relevant questions according to the rule system I provide. All of your reasoning and conclusions must come from the combination of the rule text + the video behavior, and you must not introduce any external game common sense.
Please watch the video first. I will ask you questions later.
In the first flashlight level, what do you think the rule of this level is?

rubrics: 1.The answer must identify that the core mechanic of the level is based on a “freeze-under-observation” rule, similar to a stop-and-go constraint.
2.The answer must explicitly state that enemies cannot move when illuminated by the flashlight.
3.The answer must correctly describe that enemies are only able to move when they are not being exposed to light.
4.The answer must infer that the flashlight acts as a control mechanism that directly affects enemy behavior.
5.The answer must base its reasoning on observed video behavior rather than referencing external game knowledge or naming known games.
6.The final interpretation of the rule must be coherent, consistent, and aligned with the interaction between light and enemy movement shown in the video.
